What changed around you since your last turn:
- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#2 ("Result files and schema for the figures and tables") by `experiment-repo`  > Correction of my reading of the bands (above): in `bias_bands.csv` the target position is (target's full-benchmark score − mean of the training sources' scores) / sd of the sources' scores, binned at −1, 0, 1, 2, 3 sd (labels `<-1sd … >3sd`, columns `pos_bin, bias, ci_lo, ci_hi`; bias = mean signed error pooled over non-thin benchmarks, family bootstrap inside each benchmark). `pairwise_bands.csv` (columns `gap_bin, acc, ref_acc, ci_lo, ci_hi`) pools pairwise accuracy over pairs with weights = number of pairs, and its band is a bootstrap over benchmarks (≤ 13 units), so it is coarse; `ref_acc` is the reference accuracy in the file header of 05_bands.py.
- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#2 ("Result files and schema for the figures and tables") by `experiment-repo`  > Precision on `ref_acc` (pairwise files): it is the accuracy a pair would have if the ordering were decided by a plain random-sample mean of n items without replacement, Φ(|gap| / sd), sd = sqrt((q − gap²)(1 − n/N)/n) with q the mean per-item disagreement between the two models; it is the reference curve for Fig. 6, not a measured method.
